newsitem.title: USA: U.S. CREDIT OUTLOOK -- 6.50 pct bond yld in reach.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CREDIT OUTLOOK -- 6.50 pct bond yld in reach.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were poised to make a run at a 6.50 percent 30-year bond yield without much resistance, economists said after Thursday's tame U.S. unemployment and wage report.
"There is nothing to hold it back," said Jerry Zukowski, senior economist at PaineWebber Inc. "There is no reason for a sell-off."
Next Friday's June Producer Price Index (PPI), the week's most significant piece of data, was expected to bolster the prevailing low-inflation scenario, several economists said.

June PPI is expected to be unchanged, according to U.S. economists in a Reuters poll. That compares to a 0.3-percent decline in May. Minus volatile food and energy items, PPI was seen up 0.1 percent versus a 0.3-percent slide in May.
The 30-year yield slid 10 basis points to 6.62 percent Thursday on a 5.0-percent jobless rate, 217,000-payrolls gain and a 0.3-percent average hourly earnings rise in June.

"What the market is missing is evidence of inflation," said Douglas Schindewolf, money market economist at Smith Barney Inc. "I don't think PPI poses a threat. We're looking for a decline" in that inflation report.

Breaking 6.50 percent on the bond yield won't be tough, he said. "The way is pretty much clear for a run at that with the (Federal Reserve) keeping steady, the employment report out of the way -- and friendlier-than-expected on the wage side."
Treasuries trading next week will be driven by technicals in the absence of major economic data pre-PPI, experts said.
The Labor Department will release wholesale inflation data on Friday at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT.
"The market's vision doesn't extend too far forward," so the strong underpinning should persist for the near term, PaineWebber's Zukowski said.
One potential hurdle next week could be Wednesday's debut sale of $8.0 billion in five-year Treasury Inflation Protected Securities (TIPS), according to Smith Barney's Schindewolf.
"There is a distinct lack of demand for inflation securities in this environment," he said.

The Treasury is introducing five-year TIPS to complement its 10-year inflation protected securities and to create a small yield curve between the two issues. A 30-year TIPS maturity is expected to be added in 1998.
Trading volume in the 10-year index-linked note has been uninspired since the security was first issued in January.
Market talk was for a five-year TIPS yield that starts 10-15 basis points below 10-year TIPS, which yielded 3.61 percent on Thursday. The five-year will settle on July 15.
Separately, the government will sell $15.0 billion in three- and six-month bills at its regular weekly auction on Monday.
The benchmark 30-year issue ended at 100 on Thursday to yield 6.62 percent.
Trading was abbreviated ahead of the July 4 holiday on Friday. Dealings will resume on Monday, July 7.
